title: Jobber vs Housecall Pro vs ServiceTitan for teams under five
summary: Comparing Jobber, Housecall Pro, and ServiceTitan for a team under five? See how pricing and marketing tools stack up, plus a fourth option built for growth.
body_markdown:
If you run a home service business with fewer than five people (say a two-person HVAC crew or a solo plumbing operation), you're probably wearing many hats: technician, dispatcher, and marketer. So you start looking at field service management software to make your life easier, and you’re probably bumping into three names: Jobber, Housecall Pro, and ServiceTitan.


You can rule ServiceTitan out immediately. This FSM platform is built for larger operations with dedicated dispatchers and enough job volume to justify a learning curve and an implementation cost that can run into the tens of thousands before a technician even opens the app. Jobber and Housecall Pro are both solid for day-to-day operations, but neither is built for marketing or lead gen.


Topline Pro is another tool worth considering. It covers core job management a small crew needs, but it also offers marketing and lead gen that the other tools miss.


## Jobber vs. Housecall Pro vs. ServiceTitan vs. Topline Pro - comparison table


‍


Jobber Housecall Pro ServiceTitan Topline Pro


**Pricing** Starts at $29/month for one user, scaling to $399+/month for a 5-user team No public pricing No public pricing; ServiceTitan uses custom per-technician pricing, and implementation costs add to the subscription Starts at $159/month, up to $239/month on the Pro plan


**Best for** Small crews that want straightforward job management and a built-in CRM Small crews that need strong dispatching and GPS tracking Larger operations with 20+ technicians and dedicated office staff Small crews that want job management plus built-in marketing and lead gen


**Scheduling and dispatch** Online booking, route optimization, and a customer portal (Client Hub) for quote approval and payment Drag-and-drop dispatch board, automated reminders, and live GPS tracking Dispatch board with capacity planning, technician performance reporting, and a flat-rate pricebook App-based scheduling with automated customer follow-up


**Marketing and lead gen** Marketing Suite is a $99/month add-on, included only on the Plus plan Website and review management are included; deeper tools like the sales proposal builder sit on higher plans Marketing Pro is a separate add-on starting around $500/month, best for shops with dedicated ad budgets Included on every plan: managed website, SEO, social posting, and review requests and lead tracking with marketing attribution


**Integrations and payments** QuickBooks Online sync, job costing, and online payment processing QuickBooks Online sync, recurring billing, and financial reporting QuickBooks Online and Desktop integration, payment processing, and an open API for custom integrations Built-in payment processing; QuickBooks online sync available


**Mobile app** Handles quoting, scheduling, and invoicing from the field; a few tools like Pipeline are desktop-only Handles day-to-day dispatch and job tracking from the field; some deeper reporting sits on desktop Handles field documentation and job updates; office-side dispatching and reporting are built for a desktop workflow Built mobile-first: quoting, scheduling, invoicing, and lead follow-up (Prospect Feed, Sales Assistant) all run through a conversational app, so there's no separate desktop workflow


**Ease of setup** Beginner-friendly, teams can be running within days Straightforward, though most small teams need the Essentials plan rather than Basic to get QuickBooks sync and GPS Mandatory onboarding with no self-serve option; implementation can take months Managed setup with no separate marketing tool to configure


## ServiceTitan: Built for a bigger operation


ServiceTitan is the most capable platform of the three, but it’s too much software for a small team. It's designed around dedicated dispatchers, office staff, and technician headcounts in the double digits. It has tools like capacity planning and Titan Intelligence reporting that assume there's someone whose job is managing that data.


As one contractor put it on[Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/HVAC/comments/1c4g3pi/comment/nfl0ypu/) , "ServiceTitan can do everything, but it's like giving a Ferrari to someone who just needs a pickup truck." ServiceTitan itself doesn't publish pricing, ServiceTitan itself doesn't publish pricing. It uses a custom per-technician pricing model, and implementation costs add to the subscription on top, with mandatory onboarding that typically runs several months.


Onboarding will typically take several months, and[several BBB complaints](https://www.bbb.org/us/ca/glendale/profile/project-management-software/servicetitan-inc-1216-1290182/complaints) describe contracts with early termination fees running into the tens of thousands when the software wasn't fully live. Reviewers on Capterra and G2 also point to a steep learning curve, useful for a large HVAC or plumbing operation training dedicated staff on the system, but a lot to take on for an owner who's also the one on the truck.


ServiceTitan is a great tool, but it’s a mismatch for a crew of two or three. You’re better off considering some of the ServiceTitan alternatives instead.


## Jobber: Built for job management


Jobber is built to get a small crew off paper, spreadsheets, and manual inputting. The Core plan starts at $29 a month for one user and includes quoting, scheduling, online booking, and invoicing. It has a client-facing hub that lets customers approve quotes and pay online. Setup is quick enough that most small teams are running within days.


Marketing functionality is available, but this is where the cost starts to creep up. Marketing Suite is an add-on built to bring in new work through campaigns and outreach and costs $99 per month. It is included in Jobber’s Plus plan, which starts at $399 a month for five users.


None of this makes Jobber a poor fit for day-to-day job management. It just means there are[alternatives to Jobber](https://www.toplinepro.com/blog/jobber-alternatives) that offer marketing and lead-gen built directly into the system at no extra cost.


## Housecall Pro: Built for dispatch


Housecall Pro leans hardest into dispatch and field visibility. Instead of listing fixed prices, Housecall Pro walks visitors through a series of questions about team size and needed features, then generates a custom quote. Because of that, most small teams end up needing to upgrade past the Basic tier to get flat-rate pricing, employee GPS tracking, and QuickBooks Online sync. The Essentials tier includes flat-rate pricing, employee GPS tracking, and QuickBooks Online sync, which are all tools Basic doesn't include. The drag-and-drop calendar and live technician map are great for dispatchers who need to see who's nearby when a job comes in.


A managed website and review management come standard on every plan. But to get access to lead-gen tools, like the Sales Proposal Tool and Pipeline, you have to pay for the MAX tier or separate add-ons.


One IT consultant and business owner[noted](https://www.capterra.com/p/140363/HouseCall-Pro/#Capterra___4717436) that Housecall Pro "can be somewhat pricey, especially for small enterprises that might not need all of its features.” Another[reviewer](https://www.capterra.com/p/140363/HouseCall-Pro/#Capterra___6402048) described their pricing and cost per lead as “deceptive” and that “many of the provided leads where \[sic\] junk and they still charged us hundreds of dollars for them even when they did not pan out.”


Housecall Pro is solid for a small crew that needs strong dispatching, but if marketing and lead gen matter more than dispatch tools, there are Housecall Pro alternatives out there that might be worth considering.


## Topline Pro: Built for growth beyond word-of-mouth


Topline Pro covers the same core job management the other three offer. It’s great for quoting, scheduling, customer management, invoicing, and payments. Plus, every plan comes with a managed website, ongoing SEO content, social posting, and automated review requests. This is the same work that would require separate add-ons or higher tiers with the other tools. Pricing starts at $159 a month on the Starter plan, up to $239 a month on Pro.


Topline Pro’s[Prospect Feed](https://www.toplinepro.com/get-work) scans local platforms like Nextdoor for homeowners asking for services in a contractor's area, and[Showcases](https://youtu.be/a8E1Tb2JtyM?si=8LdjpUa3w5B1btcH) turns a few job photos into a polished project page with an integrated booking form. When a lead comes in, the Sales Assistant follows up by text to fill in anything missing, like photos or job details, before a quote goes out. From there, quoting, scheduling, invoicing, and payment all happen in the same system.


We built Topline Pro for owners who've outgrown word-of-mouth but don't want SEO, social posts, reviews, and lead follow-up turning into another job at night. Jose Santiago Jr.[said that Topline Pro](https://share.google/XwcqjlWvkGNI6s8rn) "has brought me in so much more work than I could've ever dreamed of."
